title: Smooth morphisms are universally locally acyclic
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $f$ is universally locally acyclic [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]: for every scheme morphism $S'\to S$, every geometric point $\bar x'$ of $X'=X\times_S S'$, and every positive integer $n$ prime to its residue characteristic, the base-change morphism $X'\to S'$ is locally acyclic at $\bar x'$ relative to $\underline{\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z}$. In particular $f$ itself is locally acyclic. Neither properness nor a bound on the relative dimension is assumed.

proof.text: It suffices to prove local acyclicity for every smooth morphism: for an arbitrary $S\prime\to S$, the base change is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), and the definition [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf] then upgrades that assertion to universal local acyclicity. We therefore fix a smooth $f$, a geometric $\bar x$, its image $\bar s$, and $n\geq1$ prime to the residue characteristic at $\bar x$.

The injection of residue fields $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ gives the same characteristic. In an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $s$, $n$ is not in the prime of $s$; replace $S$ by the affine basic open $D(n)\subset U$ and $X$ by its inverse image. Smoothness is preserved by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). This replacement does not change either strict henselization or their map: every pointed etale neighbourhood can be refined by an affine open around its marked point lying over these opens. The full subcategories of such neighbourhoods are initial by [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1), so their ring colimits [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] and canonical maps [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](4) agree. Consequently the fibre and restriction map in the definition of local acyclicity are unchanged. Now $S$ is affine and $n$ is invertible everywhere on it.

proof.text: Fix any $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}K\to A=S_{(\bar s)}$, without an algebraicity restriction, and compose with $A\to S$ to obtain $g$. The source is affine and the now affine target is quasi-separated, so $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Take $M=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ and $F=\underline M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Its geometric stalks are $M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], hence every stalk is torsion of order dividing the now invertible $n$. Applying [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] to $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ proves that $f^{-1}R^qg_*F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}F$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-strict-local-cohomology], the exchange isomorphism gives the canonical isomorphism $H^q(A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K,F)\to H^q(B\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K,F)$ for $B=X_{(\bar x)}$. The selected $\bar t$ supplies the map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to A$ required in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-geometric-fibre-test]; its equivalence therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $H^q(\operatorname{Spec}K,F)\to H^q(B\times_A\operatorname{Spec}K,F)$. This last fibre product is precisely the vanishing-cycle fibre $V$ in [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf].

proof.text: The field $K$ is algebraically closed, hence separably closed; as a local ring with maximal ideal zero it is henselian (the idempotent-lifting condition modulo zero is tautological), hence strictly henselian. Also $n$ is invertible in $K$. Thus [sbc-lem-strict-henselian-constant-cohomology] applied to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ gives zero cohomology in every positive degree. Its degree-zero identification with $M$ is the constant-section map: the germ map is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk], and its composite with the constant-section map is the isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. The pullback coefficient on $V$ is $\underline M_V$ by [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. To identify the map on sections, use the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction [def-constructible-constant] and the inverse-image adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For any $p:Z\to W$, their composite identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(p^{-1}\underline M_W,H)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\Gamma(Z,H))$, since $\Gamma(W,p_*H)=\Gamma(Z,H)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Consequently the canonical inverse comparison $\underline M_Z\to p^{-1}\underline M_W$ of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] transposes to the section map $M\to\Gamma(W,\underline M_W)\to\Gamma(Z,p^{-1}\underline M_W)$, the second arrow being the inverse-image unit. Under the comparison this is the unit $M\to\Gamma(Z,\underline M_Z)$ of the constant-sheaf adjunction. Thus pullback along $V\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ sends the constant section $m$ to the constant section $m$. We conclude $H^q(V,\underline M_V)=0$ for $q>0$, and $M\to H^0(V,\underline M_V)$ sending $m$ to its constant section is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For completeness this is the required canonical $\alpha$, not merely an abstract isomorphism. The constant-section map $M\to(\underline M_X)_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf], $\alpha$ first takes the unique strict-local section with that germ, then restricts it to $V$. The lift of $\bar x$ to the strict-local closed point is given by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1). The compatibility formula of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] identifies the germ of a pulled-back constant section with its original germ. Therefore the section with germ $m$ is the constant section $m$, by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] and [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant]. Apply the adjunction calculation in step 5, using [def-constructible-constant], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the canonical comparison of [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], first to $B\to X$ and then to $V\to B$: in each case the unit pullback of the constant section $m$ is the constant section $m$ under that comparison. Thus its restriction is constant $m$. Thus $\alpha$ composed with $M\cong(\underline M_X)_{\bar x}$ is the isomorphism in the preceding step. As $\bar t$, $\bar x$ and $n$ were arbitrary, $f$ is locally acyclic. Step 1 proves universal local acyclicity, with no properness or dimension hypothesis.
